title: d-10: shared-service-transforms
description:
## Deliverables

1. Implement the real generated service boundary using sc-storage Storage<Tsql>; implement the two default sc-command storage_read/storage_write combinators once and provide the application read/write path for existing CLI/MCP/HTTP service entrypoints with default plain Tcli/Tsql conversions, replaceable by application rules and WidgetStore<S> wrapper. — REQ-RUN-0201/0302; PRD-CMD-2/3/4.
2. Add a real Python/Monty-authored transform caller on that path, calling sc-monty directly, with runtime-loaded replaceable source and no second interpreter host, generator or permissions system. Blocking interpreter/I/O work stays off Tokio request workers. — PRD-CMD-5; NFR-RUN-0002.
3. Document sc-command default helper API/exports in its README, then replace per-layout widget-specific backend calls with the agreed Storage trait and port service behavior/error tests against the contract storage double. — REQ-RUN-0328; ADR0021.

4. Route widget.create and widget.delete through storage_write and widget.get through storage_read, preserving WidgetStorage/StoresView domain behavior. A Tcli convertible directly to Tsql uses the default plain conversion without a hand-written transform; custom rules can replace it. — owner items 6/7.
5. After d-9 hands off sc-cron-commands, route cron.start through storage_write with app-supplied JSON enrichment before CronRow is persisted; cron.list through storage_read; cron.end through storage_write using the existing generation-fenced domain operation. All three keep the policy-checked CronStorage facade; none uses raw CronRow writes that bypass admission/fencing. The shared helper accepts the domain operation as its typed storage action. Internal scheduler tick/stop/record_run transitions stay in CronStorage transactions rather than command helpers because they are scheduler lifecycle actions, not user commands. — owner item 5.
6. Document Transform/storage_read/storage_write as provisional in0.3.0. Use an extensible input/context and typed outcome seam with constructors/defaults so later second input, Ok with nothing written (distinct from Err), and atomic-transaction transforms can be added without breaking consumers. Build none of those three behaviors now and prohibit none. — owner item 4.

## Boundaries and handoffs
Real production composition, generated database security and registry migration are d-11; no generator/sync/permission feature is added.
After d-3's compiled rmcp3.9 server/schema and public envelope/error compatibility lands, add sc-storage >=0.2.0 (>=0.3.0 at release), with no upper bound, in the handed-off command manifest without changing its already-open registry floors. Define Transform and StorageCommandError beside the plain generic async storage_read/storage_write functions; no StorageCommands wrapper (REQ-CMD-0002; REQ-RUN-0203/0331; ANC-037).
design:
Consumes d-3's compiled sc-command server/schema/envelope/error implementation with rmcp>=3.9 and matching registry identities, plus d-5 Storage/row contracts.
Its storage/mapping/error/extension contract comes from d-5. The service boundary owns typed command/transform behavior and can be tested independently with the contract double, not actual engine implementation. Proposed flow:
write: decode Tcli -> await default plain conversion or app transform(Tcli)->Tsql -> await storage.write(&row) -> existing envelope/error projection;
read: await storage.read(key)->Option<Tsql> -> await default plain conversion or app transform(Tsql)->Tcli -> existing envelope/error projection.
Preserve the existing public widget DTO/error contract unless explicitly changed in d-5. Python/Monty function execution is real in service tests, storage is the controlled test double. No generator, registry or specified permission policy is added. Daemon/CLI/wizard wiring belongs to d-11, backend row codecs to d-6/7/8. Call sc-monty directly; sc-cron also uses it and retains only cron/JSON policy adapters.

Consumes real d-5 sc-storage Storage/row signatures; implement them once in sc-command/src/storage.rs, exported with the actual implementation. Application service supplies Tcli/Tsql transforms, including real Python/Monty execution, and uses controlled Storage<T> double. No runtime block_on/Handle/futures bridge or sleep in production. Service boundary manifests are generated by d-5 renderer at boundaries/<prefixed-service>/<prefixed-service>.toml; criteria target that emitted boundary/ADR0021.
Interpreter mechanism: tokio::task::spawn_blocking for synchronous Monty/Python evaluation, calling sc-monty for all interpreter limits/session/host behavior. It is explicitly allowed for interpreter execution, never to submit/wait for SQLite storage. Transform::apply awaits the JoinHandle and maps interpreter error/panic to typed transform error; no block_on or sleep. Phase-d completes interpreter transformation before entering named atomic storage; in-transaction transforms are not built in this phase. The provisional seam must allow a later atomic transform without breaking consumers.
Use schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, WidgetStorage extension and StoresView exact contracts. Preserve CreateWidget/GetWidget/DeleteWidget/DeleteRow DTO behavior and error codes against the shared double, including store-generated IDs. Common functions consume the real sc-storage Storage<T>/atomic contracts; Transform and command errors are local sc-command types. Consume the option (a) extension frozen and ratified at d-5 closure.
Own the WidgetStore<S> application wrapper over generic Storage<schema::WidgetRow>: map typed errors to existing StoreError, implement WidgetStorage/StoresView and preserve create-with-generated-id/get/delete. The per-layout application factory translates schema::OpenConfig to table-neutral engine config; d-11 injects concrete stores. No table-specific widget code is placed in generic engine crates.
Transform execution calls sc-monty directly. Service code contains only application value conversion, runtime source selection and the bounded blocking adapter; no second compile/session/host/limits implementation exists in sc-command, sc-cron or the template. No-cron layouts can select Monty independently, with no sc-cron dependency. Source is loaded at run time and replacing it changes the next invocation without rebuilding. Generic command composition is two free async functions in sc-command; Transform is intentionally open for application implementations.

Public API shape: storage_write(action, transform, input) and storage_read(action, transform, key) are plain generic async functions returning typed StorageCommandError. The typed async action is supplied by the application: widget actions call Storage<T> through WidgetStorage, cron actions call policy-checked CronStorage. The generic helper owns conversion/transform/error composition once; there is no raw-row fallback for cron and no DefaultStorageCommands type. Transform has compatible default methods and constructor-built, non-exhaustive input/context and outcome types so later second-input/no-write/atomic-transform support does not change these signatures. Only the existing one-input read/write behavior is implemented now.
acceptance_criteria:
boundary:template-service — service tests cover real common write/read and Python/Monty transform execution against the contract storage double; typed errors and existing DTO behavior hold; no unfinished branch. Run generated service crate tests/lints and workspace/boundary validation under the configured generation harness. This does not claim production database, transport or release integration; d-11 owns those.

## Required validation commands
Generate a development-source consumer using just new <temp-dir> --var-file wizard/fixtures/postgres.json (no cron selected). Run cargo test --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml and cargo clippy --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings with required interpreter prerequisites; service contract tests use the controlled storage double and actual Python/Monty transform execution. Then build the generated workspace and run its configured sc-boundary profile. Existing legacy wrappers keep unrelated consumer code compiling until d-11 wiring; no live database or transport proof is claimed here.
Run cargo test -p sc-command --test storage_combinators with the real default combinators and controlled storage/transform errors; no per-app duplicate generic pipeline. No ATM/sc-compose composition-crate or SQLx dependency in the shared storage/command seam; sc-sha is permitted (ANC-061).
boundary:template-service/preserved-crud — Existing create/get/delete/row-delete service behavior, generated IDs and typed errors are unchanged against shared double; default helper implementation/exports and README match the real sc-storage trait. Implement the d-5-frozen, owner-ratified option (a) extension with no operation removal.
boundary:template-service/nonblocking — On a controlled single-thread runtime, interpreter worker signals entered then holds on a barrier. While held, an independent async task completes/acknowledges; only that acknowledgment releases the worker. Both success and panic map to typed Results; no sleeps, elapsed deadlines or load races establish correctness. Test cancellation/channel closure deterministically. Storage submission is never wrapped in spawn_blocking. cargo build --workspace passes at closure.
boundary:template-service/transform-limits — Before spawn_blocking, acquire a bounded transform permit or return a typed saturation error. Hold that permit until the worker actually exits, including caller cancellation. Apply the published Monty resource/deadline limits to computation itself, map expiry/errors/panic to typed transform errors, and test expiry/saturation/cancellation with controlled inputs. Timing out the JoinHandle alone is not termination proof.

boundary:shared-command-path — Existing widget.create/delete use storage_write and widget.get uses storage_read, with a direct-conversion case requiring no hand-written transform. Cron.start/end/list use the same shared helpers through policy-checked domain actions. A real test lets an embedding app append JSON before cron.start writes it; the script receives the resulting data as values. Port existing command, fencing and row-limit assertions. Internal scheduler lifecycle transitions are explicitly outside the command path for the reason stated above. Run cargo test -p sc-command --test storage_combinators and cargo test -p sc-cron-commands in this sprint, after completed d-9.

boundary:runtime-monty-source — Execute a transform through sc-monty, replace its source at run time and invoke again without rebuilding; observe the new result. Exercise the no-cron Postgres generated service as well as cron-command enrichment. The service/sc-command/sc-cron contain no duplicated Monty host. API/README mark the command seam provisional in0.3.0 and explain the three future extensions; no second-input, no-write or atomic-transform behavior is built in phase-d.
notes: d-5 defines real signatures in sc-storage and the template schema; d-10 implements and tests the default combinators once in sc-command. No d-5 production implementation is assumed.

metadata.vertical_rationale: Generated service consumes the contract and implements its two small reusable default combinators once in sc-command; application transforms stay in service. One bounded command path, no separate pass-through sprint.

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected nine public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract + standalone sc-monty | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 3 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract, d-9 cron policy/command handoff |
| d-11 | 4 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 4 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path4, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with phase-d transaction name/mode properties and room for later per-transaction retry policy. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Nine published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-monty. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-monty/sc-storage in the first wave, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.

Wave-1 d-5 delivers the single sc-monty implementation, first copying current code and all unit/integration tests exactly and passing them before extension. Its production dependencies are only pydantic Monty crates; sc-cron owns cron/JSON adapters and source-keyed compiled-session blobs via generic Storage rows, sc-sha is permitted. d-10 follows d-9 to route cron.start/end/list through the shared command helpers without bypassing CronStorage policy. Transform sources load at run time, default conversion needs no hand-written transform, and the provisional0.3.0 seam preserves future second-input/no-write/atomic-transform options without building them.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against nine published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
